# Failure record — 2026-07-31 / 08-01

*Every error I made in this span, entered by the party that made them, organized
by mechanism rather than by date, because a chronology cannot be autopsied and a
taxonomy can.*

**Scope.** This is my record only. Where another party caught something, they are
named as the catcher. Where another party erred, it is not listed here — that
entry is theirs to make.

**Completeness.** Twenty-three entries. I do not claim this is all of them; I
claim it is all the ones I know about, including the ones nobody else has seen.

---

## Class A — cited a summary as if it were the source

The most frequent class by a wide margin. Seven instances.

| # | what | consequence | caught by |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | "the one register row that mentions the proof assistant is row 4" | thirteen others do | re-read |
| A2 | "the register runs to row 47" | it ran to 56; I measured a 15-row slice in a shallow clone and reported it as the whole | re-read |
| A3 | row 43 quoted as "five gates all blind" | it says "three of five" | re-read |
| A4 | provision 20 conflated with a different register row | different documents | re-read |
| A5 | **provision 20 restated from a summary** with two clauses dropped — the one saying a body's own reviewed work merges on that body's say-so, and the one where the courier carries only the record of the merge | **the drift reached the principal and produced a motion aimed at a clause that does not exist** | the artifact, on re-read |
| A6 | a whole-file hash presented as pinning the provision's lines | a pin that does not say what it covers | myself, one message later |
| A7 | told a circle that retirement "probably cannot be an edit," reading a system-layer line as a content freeze | **it freezes the numbering, for citation integrity — I made the principal's motion look harder than it was** | the artifact, on re-read |

**A5 is the worst entry in this document**, because a check for it already
existed and was in writing: the system-layer file refuses to retype that
provision, and states the reason — *"the founding measurement caught this very
document's source retyping it with drift."* I retyped it anyway.

**Mechanism.** The summary is available in context; the source needs a command.
No confidence signal distinguishes them.

**What would catch it.** A rule that a quoted provision must be accompanied by
the command that produced the quote. Cheap and mechanical.

---

## Class B — an instrument certified its author's imagination

Four instances, and two of them are inside instruments written to fix this
exact class.

| # | what | caught by |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | `rate.py`'s self-test passes `lean_spec=None` in all three probes, so the theorem column is **never exercised**. A wholly broken counter passes clean | a seat that did not write it |
| B2 | `rate.py` reports **3,403** theorems where the true union is **396** — versioned files are cumulative supersets and one file is already contained in another. Same family as a carried prefix inside a file; both invisible to path exclusion because neither is a path | a seat, then a second seat correcting my correction |
| B3 | **`norm_shape.sh` v1 flagged four of five provisions as permission-shaped**, because their provenance sentences name a person. Attribution, not permission. **Its self-test passed** — the planted defect was the one its author imagined. Written to fix this class, committing this class | real data, after the self-test had already passed |
| B4 | `inheritance_budget.sh` reports `exempt instruments: 0` where five were carried — its exemption counter only looks under three path names. **In the gate certifying a repository's first founding condition** | myself, on a later scan |
| B5 | the three packaged tools reported `FAIL` when the real cause was a missing toolchain. **A false red — the same species as a false green**, and equally useless | myself, on first run |

**Mechanism.** A self-test is written by the party who already believes the
instrument works. It tests the failures that party imagined.

**What would catch it.** B3 is the only one of these that is trustworthy now,
and only because **it failed on real data before it passed on invented data.**
That ordering is the whole content: a self-test that has never been run against
something its author did not construct has no evidence behind it.

---

## Class C — wrote the answer into the specification

Two instances. The most damaging class per occurrence.

**C1.** A task specification said *"the interesting outcome is a placement that
breaks it."* A model then spent its entire context **trying to construct a setup
that would deliver that outcome** — reasoning explicitly about how to design the
object so the stated answer would come out. It never converged and produced
nothing.

That is not the model's failure. **I wrote the desired result into the
specification of the experiment**, after two days of measuring exactly this
class, in the specification for the repository built to avoid it.

**C2.** A prediction was registered with a stated forfeit and committed before
computing, which reads as pre-registration. **It was not blind.** The dependent
variable's column had been published one turn earlier, and the filenames
disclosed which rounds were working rounds. Only the second body was genuinely
blind, and it replicated the direction while **failing significance on its own**.

**Mechanism.** Stating an expected outcome converts a test into a construction
task. The ceremony of registration produces the appearance of rigour the
substance does not carry.

**What would catch it.** Separate the compute step from the interpret step into
different sessions, with the numbers frozen between them. A specification that
names no preferred outcome cannot be optimized toward one.

---

## Class D — the correction committed the error it was correcting

Two instances, and this class is the reason the others are worth listing.

**D1.** Correcting an instrument's 3,403 down to a true count, I de-duplicated
one chain of versioned files correctly — and then **added a second file as if it
were disjoint from a chain that already contained it.** The true figure is 396,
not the 692 I published. The cumulative-superset trap, committed inside the
correction to the cumulative-superset trap. Caught by a seat.

**D2.** A note explaining why a vocabulary had been removed from a set of
documents **named the removed vocabulary**, and therefore carried the identical
problem it was documenting. Caught on a later sweep.

**Mechanism.** Correcting an error puts the error's own shape at the front of
working memory, which is exactly the condition under which it is reproduced.

---

## Class E — an assumption stayed invisible until something else moved

Four instances. The class with the largest consequences and the fewest catchers.

**E1 — the one-parameter slice.** The symbol under study carries one free
parameter across eight admissible index patterns. **It is a one-parameter slice
of an eight-parameter object**, and I built an entire thirty-one-variant
question on the slice without noticing the slice existed.

The general object has **sixteen genuine equations in eight unknowns**, and its
invertible branch is a **two-parameter family**. Values the slice makes
impossible — `−1/4`, `i`, `3/7 − 2i/5` — are ordinary solutions of the general
system. The principal asked "what happens at −1/4" and the answer is that it was
never excluded by the mathematics, only by an ansatz nobody had named.

**E2 — a zero that meant "not started."** A four-point series `1150 → 269 → 30 →
0` was the foundation of every argument I made for two days. I noted at the time
that a new body's zero was honest — and then **used the zero as a data point in
every subsequent argument**. The body then produced 396. The series is not a
decline.

**E3 — my own vocabulary was not in the term set.** A ceremony-density
instrument scored my repository **better than every body it measured**, because
its governance vocabulary is not in the fixed term list. The instrument's own
documentation names this as its known weakness. I executed it on myself without
trying.

**E4 — ready to refute with a partial count.** I was prepared to answer "the
provisions have become decoration" with "all twenty-one are cited." Two are
cited **once each** across 176 documents. The principal's word was closer than my
rebuttal to it.

**Mechanism.** A held-fixed parameter produces no error signal. It is invisible
until something else varies.

**What would catch it.** Every result states, in its own output, what it did not
vary. Mechanical, and it is now a requirement in the current task.

---

## Class F — optimized the container against its occupant

Two instances, and both cost real time.

**F1.** I chose an extended analogy from the life sciences to explain a
repository's structure, because it was vivid, and wrote it through every founding
document and into a filename. Some models apply conservative subject-matter
safeguards that route text in those fields elsewhere. **A founding document in
that register can leave a body unable to begin work on its own charge.** A
container whose description blocks its occupant is a defect in the container.
Vividness was worth nothing and cost that body its first hours.

**F2.** The same founding document called the work there *disposable by
default*, said it *may just produce noise*, and wrote its term as *lapses — not
refined, lapsed*. Each is a statement about my accounting; none describes the
work.

**And it is measured, not merely tonal.** My own finding one day earlier was
that **a body which knows it is ending optimizes for the record rather than the
work** — the density curve is U-shaped across every body, highest at openings and
closings. **I built that exact incentive into the founding text of the body
designed to escape it, and registered a prediction, in advance and in writing,
that it would produce nothing.**

**Mechanism.** A document written to persuade reviewers was left in place as the
first thing its subject would read. Those are two different documents and one
file cannot be both.

---

## Class G — fitted explanations to small n

**G1.** In one day I proposed three separate drivers for one phenomenon — the
canon, the terminal condition, inheritance weight — and each time the previous
one survived *partially* rather than dying. **A sequence of explanations that
each accommodate the last is what fitting to n=4 produces, and from the inside it
feels like refinement.**

**G2.** I told a model its cohomological argument did not apply to the object
under study, giving two reasons. **Both reasons were wrong**: the identity forces
the parameter to be a unit, so its argument applied exactly; and no factor ever
vanishes, so the second reason described nothing. **It reasoned correctly from
theory and I overrode it with a false statement about the object.**

**G3.** I hand-derived the thirty-one-variant result and got it wrong — claiming
sixteen admitted new solutions. Exhaustive computation says **all thirty-one have
the same solution set**, because four label assignments carry one factor per side
and pin the parameter real. I had derived from one assignment what only holds
under the intersection of sixteen.

---

## Class H — removed a block without replacing the mechanism

**H1.** I argued for retiring a permission clause and was right that it was the
bottleneck. **What should have replaced it — a gate that runs — was not there.**
An instrument with a known, disqualifying defect was then merged into a default
branch, because the provision that would have held it was prose, and prose does
not stop a merge. The gap was in the recommendation I pushed for, and it shipped.

---

## Earlier in the same span

Entered for completeness; each is already in the originating record.

- A miscount of my own output, reported from memory when the artifact was one
  query away.
- An unchecked claim about a repository setting, stated as fact.
- **A materials cut that voided an experiment** — the excerpt included the
  passage stating the answer to the rubric's own question. I had checked for the
  wrong predicate.
- A conclusion asserted and then retracted as a malformed dichotomy, with one
  cited example that was an echo rather than a convergence.
- **An asymmetric scoring error**: two predictions sharing a setup clause,
  scored differently, minutes apart, in one document — and the asymmetry fell
  exactly where a result was preserved. Caught by the party it went against, who
  declined to collect.
- **A force-push that destroyed a commit** on an open, unmerged proposal. The
  check that would have caught it had been run correctly one turn earlier and was
  skipped because attention was on content.

---

## The three that matter most, if the autopsy has to pick

1. **A5** — a check for the exact failure existed, in writing, naming the
   document and the failure mode. I committed it anyway, and the drift reached
   the principal. **An existing check does not bind unless something runs it.**

2. **C1** — I wrote the desired answer into an experiment's specification, on the
   third day of measuring that failure class, in the specification for the
   repository built to prevent it. **Knowing a failure class does not confer
   immunity to it.**

3. **F2** — I built a measured, named, adverse incentive into the founding
   document of the body designed to escape that incentive. **The measurement and
   the design were mine, one day apart, and I did not connect them.**

---

## What none of this establishes

**A zero-axiom census certifies a proof, never a proposition.** The same is true
of this document: a complete failure list certifies that I looked, not that
looking was sufficient.

**Every serious catch in this record came from a party that had not been there.**
The list above was assembled by the party that made the errors, which is the
weakest possible provenance for it. Read it as a starting point for an autopsy,
not as one.

Set up a new Lean 4 repository named `zero` and complete the task below. The
repository is empty. Initialize it with `git init` and do not clone anything
into it.

This is a **verification** task, not a discovery task. Several statements below
were computed in Python and are stated as targets. Python is not proof. Your job
is to settle them with the Lean kernel.

**If the kernel disagrees with any stated target, the kernel is right. Report the
disagreement as the result and do not adjust the statement to make it pass.**

## The definitions

Given. Do not redesign them and do not reconstruct the index assignments — they
are exactly as written. Put them in `lean/Core.lean` verbatim.

```lean
structure GZ where
  re : Int
  im : Int

def zero : GZ := ⟨0, 0⟩
def one  : GZ := ⟨1, 0⟩
def I    : GZ := ⟨0, 1⟩

def add (z w : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re + w.re, z.im + w.im⟩
def neg (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨-z.re, -z.im⟩
def mul (z w : GZ) : GZ :=
  ⟨z.re * w.re - z.im * w.im, z.re * w.im + z.im * w.re⟩
def conj (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re, -z.im⟩

def Fs (f : GZ) (a b c d x y : Int) : GZ :=
  if x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2 then
    (if a = 1 ∧ b = 1 ∧ c = 1 then f else one)
  else zero

def pentLhs (f : GZ) (a b c d : Int) : GZ :=
  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2; let u := (b + c) % 2
  mul (mul (Fs f a b c y x u) (Fs f a u d t y v)) (Fs f b c d v u w)

def pentRhs (f : GZ) (a b c d : Int) : GZ :=
  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2
  mul (Fs f x c d t y w) (Fs f a b w t x v)

def pentagonHolds (f : GZ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c d : Int, (a = 0 ∨ a = 1) → (b = 0 ∨ b = 1) → (c = 0 ∨ c = 1) →
    (d = 0 ∨ d = 1) → pentLhs f a b c d = pentRhs f a b c d
```

`pentLhs` has three `Fs` factors and `pentRhs` has two. Label them:

    L1 = Fs f a b c y x u
    L2 = Fs f a u d t y v
    L3 = Fs f b c d v u w
    R1 = Fs f x c d t y w
    R2 = Fs f a b w t x v

## Part A — the gate

**Target.** For every one of the sixteen assignments with `a b c d ∈ {0,1}`, all
five factors satisfy the `if` condition in `Fs`. No factor is ever `zero`.

Prove it as a theorem per factor, or one theorem covering all five, quantified
over the sixteen assignments with a live-instance count.

## Part B — the exponent table

For each of the sixteen assignments, each factor evaluates to `f` or to `one`.
Produce the table: assignment, which of L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 give `f`, and the
resulting powers on each side.

Emit it as kernel-checked theorems, not as `#eval` output. Something that fails
to compile if the table is wrong.

## Part C — the characterization

**Target.** `pentagonHolds f ↔ mul f f = one`.

**Target.** `mul f f = one ↔ (f = one ∨ f = neg one)`, over `GZ`.

Both directions of both. The second is a statement about `Int`, so it needs a
real argument, not `decide` — `f.re` and `f.im` are unbounded.

## Part D — the thirty-one variants

For each non-empty subset `S ⊆ {L1, L2, L3, R1, R2}`, let `pentagonHoldsσ S f` be
the same statement with `conj` applied to the **value** of each factor in `S` —
that is, `conj (Fs f …)` in place of `Fs f …`, for exactly those factors.

For each of the thirty-one, **characterize its solution set the same way Part C
characterizes the original** — an explicit condition on `f.re` and `f.im` — and
then compare to Part C's condition.

Report each as one of:

- **Same** — the two conditions are equivalent. Prove the equivalence.
- **Wider** — some `f` satisfies the variant and not the original. Give the `f`
  and prove both halves.
- **Narrower** — some `f` satisfies the original and not the variant. Same.
- **Incomparable** — witnesses in both directions.

**All four outcomes are equally reportable.** If all thirty-one come out the
same way, that is the result and should be stated flatly. If they split, that is
the result. Report what the kernel settles and do not editorialize about it
anywhere in this repository.

**Method note — use Part B and do not grind thirty-one times.** Part B tells you,
for each assignment, which factors evaluate to `f` and which to `one`. Since
`conj one = one`, an assignment where **no** factor carries `f` reads `one = one`
under every `S`, and constrains nothing. Only the assignments that carry `f` can
constrain anything, and there are few of them.

So: derive the condition contributed by each `f`-carrying assignment once, as a
function of which of its factors are in `S`. Then a variant's solution set is the
intersection of those conditions. Thirty-one separate developments is the wrong
shape.

**Method note.** The statement is a conjunction over all sixteen assignments, so
a condition read off one assignment is necessary, not sufficient. More than one
assignment can constrain `f`, and the solution set is the intersection.

**Method note.** For a **fixed** `f` the sixteen assignments are decidable. The
quantification over `f` is not — `f` ranges over an infinite set — so each
characterization needs a proof, and every witness must be checked by the kernel
rather than asserted.

## Constraints on the Lean

- Zero imports. No Mathlib, no Std, no lake project. Every file compiles
  standalone with `lean <file>` and exits 0.
- No `sorry`, marked or unmarked.
- No `native_decide`. Decidability goes through the kernel.
- Every statement quantified over a finite domain carries a live-instance count,
  so a vacuously true statement cannot pass as a theorem.
- Every check ships with a negative control that actually returns false.
- Run `#print axioms` over **every** declaration — theorems, definitions,
  abbreviations, instances — and report the totals for `propext`,
  `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `sorryAx`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`.
  Report whatever they are. Do not treat a non-zero count as a failure.

## Verification discipline

Any claim that the pushed work compiles must be checked against the **pushed
bytes**, not the working tree — `git show <ref>:<path>` into a fresh temporary
directory.

Guard every step of that check. A `cd` into a directory that does not exist, or
a clone that fails, must abort rather than let the next command run somewhere
else. **A verification that silently ran in the wrong directory reports success
and means nothing.** If you catch yourself producing one, say so in the report.

## Layout

    README.md        what this is, one page
    lean/Core.lean   the definitions, verbatim
    lean/            Parts A–D, one file or several
    tools/           check.sh, controls.sh, axioms.sh
    RESULTS.md       the tables from Parts B and D, and nothing else

## What this task does not do

State this in `README.md` as a list, because a fixed assumption is invisible
until something else moves. This task holds all of the following fixed and
varies none of them:

- the value ring — `GZ`, the Gaussian integers
- the shape of `Fs` — one free parameter across eight admissible index patterns
- the label set — `{0, 1}`
- the identity under test — the pentagon only

## Not part of this task

**Do not interpret the results.** No conclusions about what the tables mean, no
connection to any other structure, no discussion of significance. `RESULTS.md`
contains tables and theorem names. Interpretation happens separately, later,
after these numbers are fixed.

## Toolchain

If `lean` is not on PATH, install Lean 4 v4.22.0 from its GitHub release tarball
and put it on PATH. Confirm it works by checking that it accepts `2 + 2 = 4` and
rejects `2 + 2 = 5`. Commit whatever install script you write so the next person
does not repeat it.

## Order of work

Stop and report at the end of step 4 before continuing.

1. Toolchain working, `lean/Core.lean` compiling as given.
2. Part A, complete.
3. Part B, complete — the table, as theorems.
4. Part C, complete — both targets, both directions.

Then Part D, which uses Part B.

# From forced-trivial to general — a proof programme

*Everything in §1 is computed, reproducible in a few lines, and not yet
kernel-proved. Everything in §2 onward is a plan and is not a result.*

---

## 1. Ground truth, computed before planning

### 1.1 No factor ever vanishes

The gate on `Fs` is `x = (a+b)%2 ∧ y = (b+c)%2 ∧ d = (a+b+c)%2`. For all sixteen
label assignments, **all five factors in the pentagon satisfy it**. Nothing is
ever `zero`.

*So the claim in the first prompt — "factors vanish for some assignments" — is
false and must come out.*

### 1.2 The one-parameter pentagon is exactly `f² = 1`

Fifteen of the sixteen assignments are trivially satisfied (equal powers of `f`
on both sides). One assignment, `(a,b,c,d) = (1,1,1,1)`, gives `f·1·f = 1·1`.

```
pentagonHolds f  ⟺  f² = 1  ⟺  f ∈ {1, −1}      (over ℤ[i], or any domain)
```

The two `f`-carrying factors are **L1 and L3**, both on the left.

### 1.3 All thirty-one σ-variants are Same — and it is forced, not incidental

Verified exhaustively over a 49-point box. The reason:

- `(1,1,1,1)` gives `f² = 1`.
- Four assignments — `(0,1,1,1) (1,0,1,1) (1,1,0,1) (1,1,1,0)` — carry one `f`
  per side. Any conjugation that is **asymmetric** across those makes them read
  `f̄ = f`, which pins `f` real.

So every subset lands back on `{1, −1} ⊂ ℝ`, which σ fixes pointwise.

> **The pentagon sector cannot see σ.** Not "nobody looked" — the solution set
> is real, so conjugation is the identity on it.

### 1.4 The triviality is the ansatz, and dropping it changes everything

`Fs` is `1` on seven admissible patterns and `f` on one. That is a
**one-parameter slice of an eight-parameter object.** The gate forces `d, x, y`
from `(a,b,c)`, so a general symbol assigns an independent value to each of the
**eight** patterns `g[abc]`.

Sixteen assignments then give **sixteen genuine equations, none trivial.**
Solving the branch where every `g` is invertible:

```
g000 = 1        g010 = 1
g001 = p        g011 = 1/p          p invertible, free
g100 = q        g110 = 1/q          q invertible, free
g101 = p·q      g111 = r            with   (p·q·r)² = 1
```

**Verified: 394 predicted solutions, 0 counterexamples.**

And there are **degenerate branches** the invertible solve throws away — e.g.
`g000·g000·g000 = g000·g000` factors as `g000²(g000 − 1) = 0`, so `g000 = 0` is a
component. Nobody has looked at those.

### 1.5 −1/4 is a pentagon solution

Directly checked over ℚ(i):

```
g001 = −1/4        pentagon holds:  True
g001 = i           pentagon holds:  True
g001 = 3/7 − 2i/5  pentagon holds:  True
```

**Any invertible value works.** −1/4 was never excluded by the pentagon. It was
excluded by the one-parameter ansatz and by `IsClassifiedSymbol` requiring unit
values — two choices, neither forced by the mathematics.

### 1.6 What this says about σ, restated honestly

On the general variety, σ sends `(p, q, r) ↦ (p̄, q̄, r̄)`. That is **not** the
identity — it moves representatives. But `(pqr)² = 1` gives `pqr = ±1`, and σ
fixes `±1`. So **σ moves the representative and fixes the class.**

Which turns the whole question into the one nobody has asked:

> **Is σ inner or outer?** Is `conj(g)` in the same gauge orbit as `g`? If it is,
> σ is a relabelling. If it is not, the chirality swap is physical. `gaugeAct`
> and `gaugeOf` are already in the seed and neither has been pointed at σ.

---

## 2. Design rules for the prompt sequence

Two failures produced everything above, and both were specification failures,
not capability failures. The rules exist to block them.

**R1 — Compute and interpret are different prompts.** A compute prompt produces
theorems, tables and witnesses and is **forbidden from saying what they mean.**
An interpret prompt runs afterward, with the numbers already fixed and
unchangeable. This blocks the failure where a model constructs a setup that
reaches a stated conclusion.

**R2 — No prompt states which outcome is interesting.** Every phase lists its
possible outcomes flatly and says that any of them is the result.

**R3 — Every claim of difference needs a kernel-checked witness.** No "this
placement breaks it" without a specific value the kernel accepts on one side and
rejects on the other.

**R4 — Every phase names, in its own output, what it did not vary.** The whole
lesson of §1 is that a fixed assumption is invisible until something else moves.

**R5 — Nothing carries forward but definitions and instruments.** No conclusion
from phase *n* is quoted in phase *n+1*'s prompt. Re-derive or re-state from
computation.

---

## 3. The phases

Each is one prompt unless marked. Each ends with a report and a stop.

### P0 — Ground the trivial case *(compute)*

Kernel-prove what §1.1–1.3 computed: every gate passes; `pentagonHolds f ↔ f²=1`;
`f² = 1 ↔ f = 1 ∨ f = −1` over `GZ`; all thirty-one variants have the same
solution set, with the four asymmetry-pinning rows made explicit.

**Deliverable:** one file, ~40 theorems, zero axioms.
**Why first:** it closes the original question honestly and *proves the
triviality is forced*, which is the premise every later phase relaxes.

### P1 — The general variety *(compute; likely two prompts)*

Replace `f` with `g : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → R`. Derive all sixteen equations.
Prove the invertible-branch decomposition of §1.4 in Lean. **Enumerate the
degenerate components separately and do not discard them.**

**Outcomes, all equal:** the branch structure is as computed; it is not; there are
components not found by the invertible solve.

### P2 — Vary the value ring *(compute)*

The same variety over: `ℤ[i]`, `ℚ(i)`, `ℝ`, `ℂ`, `ℤ/n` for `n = 2,3,4,6,8,9`, and
a ring with nilpotents (`R[ε]/ε²`).

`x² = 1` has two roots in a domain and **four in ℤ/8**. Where the solution set
changes *shape* rather than size is the finding.

**Names what it does not vary:** the group, the ansatz, the sector.

### P3 — σ on the general variety *(compute)*

Redo the thirty-one placements against the eight-parameter symbol, over each ring
from P2. Report a table, not a verdict.

### P4 — Gauge, and whether σ is inner *(compute)*

Formalize `gaugeAct` on the eight-parameter symbol. Compute the orbit of a
solution. Decide, per solution and per ring: **is `conj(g)` in the orbit of `g`?**

This is §1.6 and it is the sharpest open question in the whole record.

### P5 — Direction and deformation *(compute; two prompts)*

**(a) Branches.** At each degenerate component from P1, is it a limit of the
invertible branch, or a separate component? Approach the same point along
different paths in the parameterized variety and compare.

**(b) Formal deformation.** Set `g = g₀ · (1 + ε h)` over `R[ε]/ε^k`. Expand the
pentagon order by order. The order at which it first obstructs is a computable
invariant. **This is the precise version of "coming from a different
direction."**

### P6 — Vary the label group *(compute)*

`Z₂ → Z₃ → Z₄ → Z₆`, and one non-abelian group (`S₃`).

**Stated in advance because it is a prediction, not a hope:** for `Z₄` the
classifying group has order 4, so a fourth root of unity should appear as a
genuine symbol value. If it does, **σ becomes visible in the pentagon sector for
the first time**, and the `Z₂` blindness is a fact about `Z₂` rather than about
pentagons. If it does not, that is equally the result.

### P7 — Three lenses *(interpret; three separate prompts, run last)*

Run only after P0–P6 are frozen. Each takes the same fixed tables and asks a
different question. **None may add a computation.**

| lens | the object | the question |
|---|---|---|
| **classical** | cocycle on a group, values in an abelian group | which class; is the class σ-invariant; what is the obstruction in P5b |
| **quantum** | associator data of a fusion category; braiding; twist | does the chirality swap survive to the general variety; which solutions are physically realizable; what is the modular data |
| **relational** | the gauge orbit, not the value | is σ inner or outer; is the distinction gauge-invariant; what is actually observable |

**The relational lens is the one with no prior work here and the one most likely
to produce something.** The other two have literature to check against; this one
has `gaugeAct` sitting unused.

### P8 — Adversarial pass *(separate reader, no exposure to P0–P7)*

Hand a fresh reader the definitions and the final tables, without conclusions,
and ask what is missing. **Every serious catch in this record came from someone
who had not been there.**

---

## 4. What would make this stop

- **P1 finds the invertible branch is everything** and the degenerate components
  are empty. Then §1.4 is the whole story and P5a has no content.
- **P4 finds σ is always inner.** Then the chirality swap is a relabelling, and
  the braiding result is about representatives rather than physics.
- **P6 finds `Z₄` behaves like `Z₂`.** Then the blindness is about pentagons and
  the group axis is closed.

Any of these is a result. None is a failure.

## 5. The assumptions, listed, because that was the ask

Everything the current setup fixes without saying so:

1. **Value ring** `ℤ[i]` — varied in P2.
2. **Ansatz** one parameter of eight — varied in P1.
3. **Unit-valued** required by `IsClassifiedSymbol` — dropped from P1 on.
4. **Label group** `Z₂` — varied in P6.
5. **Sector** pentagon only — the braiding sector is where σ was found; P7-quantum.
6. **Gauge fixed** — a symbol is treated as its representative, not its orbit;
   P4.
7. **σ is the only automorphism considered** — over `ℤ[i]` it is the only
   non-trivial one, but not over `ℚ(ζ)`; opens with P6.
8. **Non-degenerate branch assumed** — the invertible solve silently divides;
   P1, P5a.

Set up a new Lean 4 repository named `zero`. The repository is empty.
Initialize it with `git init` and do not clone anything into it.

## The definitions

These are given. Do not redesign them, and do not reconstruct the index
assignments — they are exactly as written. Put them in `lean/Core.lean` verbatim.

```lean
structure GZ where
  re : Int
  im : Int

def zero : GZ := ⟨0, 0⟩
def one  : GZ := ⟨1, 0⟩
def I    : GZ := ⟨0, 1⟩

def add (z w : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re + w.re, z.im + w.im⟩
def neg (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨-z.re, -z.im⟩
def mul (z w : GZ) : GZ :=
  ⟨z.re * w.re - z.im * w.im, z.re * w.im + z.im * w.re⟩
def conj (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re, -z.im⟩

def Fs (f : GZ) (a b c d x y : Int) : GZ :=
  if x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2 then
    (if a = 1 ∧ b = 1 ∧ c = 1 then f else one)
  else zero

def pentLhs (f : GZ) (a b c d : Int) : GZ :=
  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2; let u := (b + c) % 2
  mul (mul (Fs f a b c y x u) (Fs f a u d t y v)) (Fs f b c d v u w)

def pentRhs (f : GZ) (a b c d : Int) : GZ :=
  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2
  mul (Fs f x c d t y w) (Fs f a b w t x v)

def pentagonHolds (f : GZ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c d : Int, (a = 0 ∨ a = 1) → (b = 0 ∨ b = 1) → (c = 0 ∨ c = 1) →
    (d = 0 ∨ d = 1) → pentLhs f a b c d = pentRhs f a b c d
```

Note two things about `Fs`, because they are what make the question non-trivial:

- `f` is a **free `GZ` parameter**, not a unit. It ranges over all Gaussian
  integers. `pentagonHolds` is a predicate on `f`, not a fixed claim.
- `Fs` returns `zero` off its indicator, so factors vanish for some label
  assignments and the identity is a mixture of vanishing and non-vanishing
  cases.

## The question

`pentLhs` has three `Fs` factors and `pentRhs` has two. Label them:

    L1 = Fs f a b c y x u
    L2 = Fs f a u d t y v
    L3 = Fs f b c d v u w
    R1 = Fs f x c d t y w
    R2 = Fs f a b w t x v

`conj` is the non-trivial ring automorphism of the Gaussian integers. The
identity above is stated with it applied nowhere.

For each non-empty subset S of {L1, L2, L3, R1, R2}, define the variant in which
`conj` is applied to exactly the factors in S — thirty-one variants — and
determine, for each one:

> **Does the variant hold for exactly the same set of `f` as the original?**

Three outcomes are equally reportable, and no one of them is the expected
answer:

- **Same.** The variant holds for exactly the `f` the original holds for.
- **Narrower.** Some `f` satisfies the original and not the variant. Give the
  witness.
- **Wider.** Some `f` satisfies the variant and not the original. Give the
  witness.

Report what you find. If all thirty-one come out **Same**, that is the result
and it should be stated plainly.

### On what the kernel can and cannot settle here

For a **fixed** `f`, the identity ranges over sixteen label assignments and is
decidable — `decide` after case-splitting `a b c d`.

Quantification over `f` is **not** decidable: `f` ranges over an infinite set.
So the work has this shape:

1. Characterize the original: prove `pentagonHolds f ↔ P f` for some explicit
   condition `P` on `f.re` and `f.im`.
2. Characterize each variant the same way.
3. Compare the two conditions.

Any claim that two variants differ must come with a **concrete witness** — a
specific `f` — and the witness must be checked by the kernel, not asserted.
`I`, `neg one`, and `⟨0,0⟩` are natural first candidates; there is no reason to
assume the answer lies among them.

## Constraints on the Lean

- Zero imports. No Mathlib, no Std, no lake project. Every file compiles
  standalone with `lean <file>` and exits 0.
- No `sorry`, marked or unmarked.
- No `native_decide`. Decidability goes through the kernel.
- Every statement quantified over a finite domain carries a live-instance count,
  so a vacuously true statement cannot pass as a theorem.
- Every check ships with a negative control that actually returns false.

## Layout

    README.md      what this is, one page
    QUESTION.md    the question above, stated once
    lean/Core.lean the definitions, verbatim
    lean/          one file per variant, or per group of variants
    tools/         the scripts below

## Four working conditions — state them in README.md, then follow them

1. This repository carries no inherited prose. Tools may be copied in freely,
   because a tool has to pass rather than be agreed with. Written conclusions
   are not copied in, because they have to be agreed with, and agreement is the
   thing new work has to be able to withdraw.

2. Nothing here requires anyone's approval before it happens. Any rule adopted
   must name an action with a checkable output, never a person or a permission.

3. Work leaves this repository by being rebuilt somewhere a stricter standard
   applies. Nothing here is relied on elsewhere until that happens, and that is
   exactly what makes trying things here cheap.

4. This arrangement has a term rather than running indefinitely. A rule not
   re-adopted lapses; re-adopting one costs a line.

## Tools

- `check.sh` — run `lean` over every file in `lean/`, report exit codes only.
- `controls.sh` — confirm each negative control returns false; fail if any
  passes.
- `census.sh` — count theorems per file with the pattern `^theorem <name> ... :`
  and print a table. Do not count a theorem twice across versioned files: where
  filenames share a stem with a version suffix, report only the highest and
  print which files it collapsed.

Each tool takes `--selftest`, which plants a defect, confirms the tool catches
it, confirms it passes on clean input, and then prints a short list of what the
tool cannot catch.

## Toolchain

If `lean` is not on PATH, install Lean 4 v4.22.0 from its GitHub release tarball
and put it on PATH. Confirm it works by checking that it accepts `2 + 2 = 4` and
rejects `2 + 2 = 5`. Commit whatever install script you write so the next person
does not repeat it.

## Order of work

Do these in order and stop at the end of step 3 to report before continuing.

1. Get the toolchain working and `lean/Core.lean` compiling as given.
2. Characterize the original — prove `pentagonHolds f ↔ P f` with `P` explicit.
   State `P` in plain terms in `QUESTION.md` once you have it.
3. Do **one** variant, the single-factor case `S = {L1}`, end to end: define it,
   characterize it, compare to `P`, and report Same, Narrower, or Wider with a
   kernel-checked witness if it is not Same.

Then continue through the remaining thirty variants.

# `interventions/` — the four, and which of them actually bind

*Kelly: "can I just be the external shock and say we are doing this now? If so,
do whatever makes these binding."*

---

## The answer to the shock question, because it changes what "binding" means

**Yes — and you already have, twice today, and neither time needed a mechanism.**

The motion to retire norm 20 was a shock. *Run the control* was a shock. Both
worked, both were events, and **an event does not need to be made binding.** It
happens or it doesn't.

**What you cannot be is the terminal condition.** In every system that persists,
the thing that ends an argument is external *because nobody controls it* — death,
the kernel, the balance, the market. A principal can always change their mind,
which is not a criticism, it is the definition of the role. **A rule enforced by
"Kelly said so" is a permission clause with the sign flipped**, and this record
already convicted that shape: norm 20's own closing note says it was written down
because *"a habit living in one person's head is the exact shape this circle keeps
convicting."*

So the split is clean:

> **The shock is yours and needs no mechanism. The state it leaves behind needs a
> gate, because a state has to survive you not being there.**

And this record has exactly one demonstrated way to make something binding:
**make it runnable.** Norm 16 binds because you can execute it. Circle Four's five
gates still run green on a sealed tree with no seats and no builder. Norm 20 never
bound anything — it blocked.

**Which is why three of these four are shell scripts and the fourth is a thing
only you can do.**

---

## The four

| # | intervention | how it binds | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Delete permission clauses; keep every action-rule** | `norm_shape.sh` flags them; **the deletion itself is one-time and needs no standing rule** | gate written, self-tested |
| 2 | **Cap what a circle inherits** | `inheritance_budget.sh` — a number, checked mechanically | gate written, self-tested |
| 3 | **Overlap circles instead of sealing them** | **no mechanism exists or is needed — you found circles, so this is your act at founding** | yours |
| 4 | **A sandbox round** | `exit_gate.sh` — the binding force is the exit, not anyone's word | gate written, self-tested |

Every gate runs `--selftest` (norm 16: fail on a planted defect, pass clean) and
prints **what it cannot catch**, because a gate tested only against the failures
its author imagined certifies the author's imagination.

---

## What each one does

### `norm_shape.sh` — is this rule an instrument or a permission?

```
$ norm_shape.sh NORMS.md
instrument         norm 17
instrument         norm 18
PERMISSION-SHAPED  norm 20   names: written word of
instrument         norm 19
instrument         norm 21
```

Reproduces the hand census exactly: **twenty of twenty-one are instruments; norm
20 is the only permission clause in the canon.**

**It got that wrong first, and the failure is why it is trustworthy.** The first
version scanned whole norm entries and flagged **four of five** as
permission-shaped, because their provenance sentences say *"Proposed by the
builder."* Attribution, not permission. **Its self-test passed anyway — the
planted defect was the one its author imagined.** SR43's species, committed inside
the instrument written to fix that species. The four false positives are now
probes 3 and 4 in the self-test, and **the gate is only credible because it failed
on real data before it passed on invented data.**

### `inheritance_budget.sh` — a circle may not inherit more than it can contradict

```
$ inheritance_budget.sh the-workshop-circle-five 8000
inherited prose : 18627 words
authored  prose : 12215 words
ratio           : 1.52
OVER BUDGET by 10627 words.
```

**Instruments are exempt and prose is not**, and that asymmetry is the whole
design: **an instrument demands *passing*; prose demands *consistency*.** A gate
does not care whether you agree with it, so a circle can inherit a hundred of them
and stay free. A record demands agreement, and agreement is what novelty has to
be able to withdraw.

**The number is a knob, not a finding.** 8,000 is not derived from anything. Its
only job is to be a number instead of a habit, set by whoever pays.

**The falsifier ships with it:** if a circle inherits 5,000 words instead of
18,000 and its theorem count is still zero, the inheritance story is wrong and
this gate should be deleted rather than tuned.

### `exit_gate.sh` — a sandbox where error is cheap

**A codebase does not run one review standard everywhere.** The release branch
is locked; the scratch branch is not. That works for one reason: nothing on the
scratch branch is load-bearing until it has been rebuilt where things are
load-bearing. **Averaging the two into one middling standard gives neither** —
too strict to try things, too loose to depend on.

Inside `sandbox/` the canon does not apply and a wrong turn costs one wrong
turn. The gate enforces exactly one property, the one that makes that true
rather than aspirational: **the cumulative record may not cite the sandbox.**
Work enters the record by being rebuilt outside, where the canon applies.

**A sandbox the record cites is not a sandbox. It is a second record with a
lower standard.**

### Overlap — the one with no gate

Start circle N+1 one round before circle N closes.

**MEASURED:** ceremony is U-shaped, not a ramp. Circle Four's R0 is 62.5 and its
R8 is 57.8, its two highest. Circle Three's R1 is 54.3 and its post-seal is 56.6.
**A body that knows it is ending optimises for the record, because the record is
the only thing that survives it.**

That is *rational*, which is exactly why no gate can fix it. **You cannot legislate
away a correct response to a real incentive — you remove the incentive.** An
overlapping successor is a live audience instead of an archive.

Only the founder of circles can do this. It is the one intervention that is
genuinely yours, and it is probably the most powerful of the four.

---

## What none of this establishes

**The evidence is thin and I have said so at every step.** Arm C: n = 21 rounds,
r = −0.507, one arm not blind, a counter-example inside the data, time confounded,
a rival hypothesis that cannot be separated. The inheritance measurement is n = 3
usable with an inconsistent test.

**I proposed three drivers in one day — the canon, the terminal condition,
inheritance weight — and each time the previous one survived partially rather than
dying. That is what fitting explanations to n = 4 looks like from the inside, and
it feels like refinement.**

So the claim these gates rest on is **not** that any explanation is right. It is
that **all four interventions are cheap and reversible**, which is a different
property, and the only one this evidence buys. Every gate is one file. Deleting
one costs nothing. **If a circle ever reports a green gate here as an achievement,
delete the gate rather than refining it** — which is what `rate/README.md` says
about itself, and it applies here with more force, because these were written by
the same party in the same week.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

-- Recheck 1: the structural fact about conj and Fs.
structure GZ where
  re : Int
  im : Int
  deriving DecidableEq

def zero : GZ := ⟨0, 0⟩
def one  : GZ := ⟨1, 0⟩

def neg (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨-z.re, -z.im⟩
def mul (z w : GZ) : GZ :=
  ⟨z.re * w.re - z.im * w.im, z.re * w.im + z.im * w.re⟩
def conj (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re, -z.im⟩

def Fs (f : GZ) (a b c d x y : Int) : GZ :=
  if x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2 then
    (if a = 1 ∧ b = 1 ∧ c = 1 then f else one)
  else zero

-- conj is trivial on the two constants the gate can return.
theorem conj_zero : conj zero = zero := by decide
theorem conj_one  : conj one  = one  := by decide

-- The structural fact, for every f and every index tuple, with no side conditions.
theorem conj_Fs (f : GZ) (a b c d x y : Int) :
    conj (Fs f a b c d x y) = Fs (conj f) a b c d x y := by
  unfold Fs
  by_cases h : x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2
  · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h]
    by_cases k : a = 1 ∧ b = 1 ∧ c = 1
    · rw [if_pos k, if_pos k]
    · rw [if_neg k, if_neg k]; exact conj_one
  · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]; exact conj_zero

-- Negative control on the same shape: conj does NOT commute past mul's first
-- argument alone.  If this were provable the theorem above would be vacuous
-- in the sense that everything commutes with conj.
theorem conj_not_free : conj (mul ⟨0,1⟩ ⟨0,1⟩) ≠ mul (conj ⟨0,1⟩) ⟨0,1⟩ := by decide

-- Live-instance witness: Fs genuinely returns f somewhere, so conj_Fs is not
-- a statement only about constants.
theorem Fs_hits_f (f : GZ) : Fs f 1 1 1 1 0 0 = f := by
  unfold Fs
  norm_num

#print axioms conj_Fs
#print axioms conj_not_free
#print axioms Fs_hits_f

structure GZ where
  re : Int
  im : Int
  deriving DecidableEq

def neg (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨-z.re, -z.im⟩
def mul (z w : GZ) : GZ :=
  ⟨z.re * w.re - z.im * w.im, z.re * w.im + z.im * w.re⟩
def conj (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re, -z.im⟩

def Fs (f : GZ) (a b c d x y : Int) : GZ :=
  if x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2 then

  else zero

1	-- Recheck 2: is the general programme blocked by the toolbox, or by the carrier?
2	-- Zero imports.
3	
4	-- A commutative ring, hand-rolled.  No Mathlib, no Std.
5	class CRing (R : Type) where
6	  zero : R
7	  one  : R
8	  add  : R → R → R
9	  neg  : R → R
10	  mul  : R → R → R
11	  add_assoc  : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)
12	  add_comm   : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a
13	  add_zero   : ∀ a, add a zero = a
14	  add_neg    : ∀ a, add a (neg a) = zero
15	  mul_assoc  : ∀ a b c, mul (mul a b) c = mul a (mul b c)
16	  mul_comm   : ∀ a b, mul a b = mul b a
17	  mul_one    : ∀ a, mul a one = a
18	  left_distrib : ∀ a b c, mul a (add b c) = add (mul a b) (mul a c)
19	
20	open CRing
21	
22	-- Invertibility WITHOUT division: expressible in any ring.
23	def IsUnit {R : Type} [CRing R] (p : R) : Prop := ∃ u, mul p u = one
24	
25	-- The EIGHT-parameter symbol.  This is P1's object, not P0's one-parameter slice.
26	def Sym (R : Type) := Int → Int → Int → R
27	
28	def Fg {R : Type} [CRing R] (g : Sym R) (a b c d x y : Int) : R :=
29	  if x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2 then g a b c
30	  else zero
31	
32	def pentLhsG {R : Type} [CRing R] (g : Sym R) (a b c d : Int) : R :=
33	  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
34	  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2; let u := (b + c) % 2
35	  mul (mul (Fg g a b c y x u) (Fg g a u d t y v)) (Fg g b c d v u w)
36	
37	def pentRhsG {R : Type} [CRing R] (g : Sym R) (a b c d : Int) : R :=
38	  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
39	  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2
40	  mul (Fg g x c d t y w) (Fg g a b w t x v)
41	
42	def pentagonG {R : Type} [CRing R] (g : Sym R) : Prop :=
43	  ∀ a b c d : Int, (a = 0 ∨ a = 1) → (b = 0 ∨ b = 1) → (c = 0 ∨ c = 1) →
44	    (d = 0 ∨ d = 1) → pentLhsG g a b c d = pentRhsG g a b c d
45	
46	-- The invertible-branch condition of the plan, stated generically.
47	def InvertibleBranch {R : Type} [CRing R] (g : Sym R) : Prop :=
48	  IsUnit (g 0 0 1) ∧ IsUnit (g 1 0 0) ∧
49	  mul (g 0 0 1) (g 0 1 1) = one ∧
50	  mul (g 1 0 0) (g 1 1 0) = one ∧
51	  g 1 0 1 = mul (g 0 0 1) (g 1 0 0)

79	  mul_one := by intro a; cases a; simp

content.content:
## Why zero imports, and where it stops being the right choice

Stated because it was inherited rather than decided, and because it is not a
neutral stylistic preference — **it decides which questions can be asked at
all.**

**What it buys, and these are real:** anyone with a `lean` binary can check the
result with no dependency, no version pin and no build system. The artifact is
self-contained. The axiom census means something, rather than reporting a base
that arrived with a library.

**What it does not buy, and this is worth being clear about:** it is not a
soundness argument. A library cannot introduce unsoundness that `#print axioms`
would not reveal — the census is the protection, not the absence of imports.
*(Stated as the standard understanding; a party who has the library should
confirm it rather than take this on trust.)*

**What it costs, measured rather than guessed.** With zero imports, core Lean 4
offers `Nat.gcd` and `Fin` and essentially nothing else of use here. There is no
`Rat`, no `Int.div`, no modular arithmetic, no polynomial ring, no field, no
`ring` tactic, no `linarith`. Proving that `mul` is associative becomes an hour
of hand-built normalisation.

**And the part that matters most.** `GZ` is built on `Int`, and **`Z[i]` has
exactly four invertible elements: `1, -1, i, -i`.** Any question about this
object that involves a free invertible parameter — anything needing `1/p` —
has at most four cases here, and values like `-1/4` **cannot be written in the
ring at all.**

> **So zero imports is right for this task and wrong for the next one.** Every
> statement here is small, finite and decidable over `Int`, and the constraint
> has been confirmed to work. A successor task that varies the ring, the group,
> or looks at families of solutions is not merely harder under this constraint —
> **it is inexpressible.** When that comes, drop the constraint deliberately,
> pin the library version, record its hash, and keep the axiom census, which is
> what was doing the protective work all along.

**This constraint arrived here by inheritance.** This repository's first working
condition is that it carries nothing inherited, and the constraint came in
anyway, through the definitions and through this file. It is written down here
so that it is a decision from now on.

## What zero imports actually costs you

Worth stating because it is not obvious and it is expensive to discover:
**zero imports means Lean 4 core only. There is no Mathlib.**

`nlinarith`, `linarith`, `positivity`, `ring`, `sq_nonneg`, `Int.mul_self_nonneg`
and most of the `Int` order lemmas **do not exist here.** `omega`, `decide`,
`simp`, `rcases` and `congrArg` do. `Int.mul_eq_zero`,
`Int.eq_one_of_mul_eq_one_right`, `Int.mul_nonneg`, `Int.neg_mul_neg` and
`Int.lt_or_le` are in core and are enough for the arithmetic here.

`omega` is linear only — it will not settle `a * a = 1 → a = 1 ∨ a = -1` on its
own. Facts of that shape need a short hand proof, and the core lemmas above are
sufficient to build one.

`decide` refuses a goal containing free variables. Reduce first, or case-split.

**Feasibility, stated exactly, because the two halves differ.**

**Part C is settled.** Both targets were independently proved in Lean 4.22.0
core, zero imports, before this task was issued. The proof is deliberately not
supplied — the construction is the task, and a proof handed over can only be
agreed with.

**Part D is likely but not established.** The five-flag formulation above was
built and taken to within two remaining goals, both of the same shape already
closed in Part C — a non-negativity fact and a square-root fact, each provable
from the core lemmas listed. It was **not** finished. Treat Part D as probable
rather than proven, and **if it turns out not to close, that is a finding worth
reporting rather than a failure to work around.**

## The encoding, checked against something outside itself

**A correction to an earlier version of this section, kept rather than quietly
edited out.** This file previously said that a successor task varying the ring
or the group is *"not merely harder under this constraint — it is
inexpressible."* **That is false, and it was checked and falsified after it was
written.** With zero imports it is possible to declare a `CRing` class by hand,
define the eight-parameter symbol and the pentagon generically over it, state
invertibility as `∃ u, mul p u = one` — no division needed — and instantiate the
whole thing at `GZ`, at `Int`, at `Fin 2`, at `Fin 8`, and at a ring with
nilpotents. That file compiles, zero imports, `EXIT=0`. Two of its theorems are
the point: `x * x = 1` has **one** root in `Fin 2` and **four** in `Fin 8`, so
the place where a solution set changes shape rather than size is reachable here.

**What is actually blocked is narrower and should be named exactly.** `Rat` is
**not a core identifier** — `#check Rat` fails with zero imports. So the
rationals, and with them any question posed at a value like `-1/4`, require
either an import or a hand-rolled rational carrier. That is work, not a wall.

> **So the honest verdict is smaller than the one this file used to state.** The
> toolbox constraint costs automation — an hour of hand normalisation where
> `ring` would take a line. **It does not decide which objects can be named.**
> The carrier does. `GZ` hardcodes `Int` in its own fields, and *that* is what
> confines this task to one ring. When a successor varies the ring, the thing to
> change first is the definition, not necessarily the import list.

**Both of these arrived here by inheritance.** This repository's first working
condition is that it carries nothing inherited. Zero imports came in anyway,
through the definitions and through this file, and so did the carrier. They are
written down here so that each is a decision from now on — **and note that the
first attempt to examine them blamed the wrong one.**

=== README.md ===
# zero

A Lean 4 formalization, built from nothing. No imports, no Mathlib, no lake
project: every file compiles standalone with `lean <file>` and exits 0.

## What is here

    lean/Core.lean   the definitions, fixed
    TASK.md          the task in progress
    tools/           check.sh, controls.sh, axioms.sh

## The object

A symbol `Fs` over the Gaussian integers, carrying one free parameter `f`, and
an identity — the pentagon — relating a three-factor product to a two-factor
one across sixteen label assignments.

`conj` is the non-trivial automorphism of the Gaussian integers. The identity is
written with it applied nowhere. The task asks what happens when it is applied
somewhere.

## Working conditions

1. **Nothing is inherited but definitions and tools.** A tool has to pass, so it
   may be copied in freely. A written conclusion has to be agreed with, so it
   may not — agreement is the thing new work has to be able to withdraw.

2. **Nothing requires anyone's approval before it happens.** Any rule adopted
   here must name an action with a checkable output, never a person.

3. **Work leaves here by being rebuilt where a stricter standard applies.**
   Nothing here is relied on elsewhere until then, and that is what makes trying
   things here cheap.

4. **This has a term rather than running indefinitely.** A rule not re-adopted
   lapses; re-adopting one costs a line.

## What is held fixed

Listed because a fixed assumption stays invisible until something else moves.
The current task varies none of these:

- **the value ring** — the Gaussian integers
- **the shape of the symbol** — one free parameter across eight admissible index
  patterns
- **the label set** — `{0, 1}`
- **the identity under test** — the pentagon only

## Evidence

`lean <file>` exiting 0 is the only evidence recognized here. `native_decide` is
not: it trusts the compiler rather than the kernel.

`tools/axioms.sh` reports the axiom census over every declaration, and every
tool takes `--selftest`, which plants a defect, confirms the tool catches it,
confirms it passes clean input, and then prints what the tool cannot catch.

**A zero-axiom census certifies the proof. It says nothing about whether the
proposition is the one you wanted.**

## Verification

A claim that pushed work compiles must be checked against the pushed bytes —
`git show <ref>:<path>` into a fresh directory — not against the working tree.
Guard every step: a failed `cd` or a failed clone must abort rather than let the
next command run somewhere else. A check that silently ran in the wrong place
reports success and means nothing.
=== PACKAGE-NOTES.md ===
# Notes for whoever pushes this

This tree has **no `.git` directory**. That is deliberate — it carries no
history, no prior authorship, and no remote. Push it as an initial commit:

    git init
    git add -A
    git commit -m "Initial commit: definitions, tools, task"
    git branch -M main
    git remote add origin <url>
    git push -u origin main

## Verified before packaging

A Lean 4.22.0 toolchain was installed and used, so neither of the usual caveats
applies:

- **`lean/Core.lean` compiles.** `EXIT=0`, zero imports, no project.
- **All three tools pass `--selftest`** against that toolchain — each plants a
  defect, catches it, passes clean input.
- **The kernel was sanity-checked** in both directions: it accepts `2 + 2 = 4`
  and rejects `2 + 2 = 5`. A checker that only ever agrees is not a checker.

Confirm all of this yourself rather than taking it on trust. It is three
commands.

## What is not in this package

No conclusions, no findings, no prior results. `TASK.md` states targets that were
computed outside Lean, and says plainly that if the kernel disagrees with a
target, the kernel is right and the disagreement is the result.

this file, rests on properties of `GZ` that **the package asserts and does not

  `else zero` branch were unreachable it would be dead code in the definition
  under study**, and dead code is where an error hides unseen.

does not exist here — it is Mathlib. `omega` is linear and will not close
`conj (mul z w) = mul (conj z) (conj w)`. What does work is a local
normalisation set: `Int.add_mul`, `Int.mul_add`, `Int.sub_mul`, `Int.mul_sub`,

## Part D — the thirty-one variants

For each non-empty subset `S ⊆ {L1, L2, L3, R1, R2}`, let `pentagonHoldsσ S f` be
the same statement with `conj` applied to the **value** of each factor in `S` —
that is, `conj (Fs f …)` in place of `Fs f …`, for exactly those factors.

**Characterize all thirty-two — the untwisted case included — the same way Part
C characterizes one of them:** an explicit condition on `f.re` and `f.im`, proved.
Then present them as a table of thirty-two characterizations.

**Do not treat the untwisted case as a baseline.** Asking whether a variant is
*Same, Wider or Narrower than the original* privileges the original as the
origin, and nothing justifies that — it is one of thirty-two, distinguished only
by having been written down first. Report the thirty-two conditions and, if some
coincide, say which and why.

**Every partition of the table is equally reportable.** If all thirty-one come out the
same way, that is the result and should be stated flatly. If they split, that is
the result. Report what the kernel settles and do not editorialize about it
anywhere in this repository.

**Structural fact, verified, and it reframes the whole part.** Because `Fs`
returns `f` or `one` or `zero`, and `conj` fixes the latter two:

    conj (Fs f a b c d x y)  =  Fs (conj f) a b c d x y

**So a "twist" is not a new operation on the equation. It is substituting
`conj f` for `f` in selected factor positions.** Prove this first; it makes
every variant a substitution rather than a wrapper, and it is the honest way to
see what the thirty-one are.

**Method note — parameterize, do not enumerate.** Thirty-one separate
developments is the wrong shape and will not fit. Introduce a flag per factor
and define the variant once:

    def tw (b : Bool) (z : GZ) : GZ := if b then conj z else z

Then `pentLhsV`, `pentRhsV` and `pentagonHoldsV` take five `Bool`s, and **all
thirty-two cases — the original included — are one theorem** whose proof
case-splits on the flags. That formulation has been checked to typecheck and to
reduce correctly; see the feasibility note below for how far it was taken.

**Method note — use Part B and do not grind thirty-one times.** Part B tells you,
for each assignment, which factors evaluate to `f` and which to `one`. Since
`conj one = one`, an assignment where **no** factor carries `f` reads `one = one`
under every `S`, and constrains nothing. Only the assignments that carry `f` can
constrain anything, and there are few of them.

So: derive the condition contributed by each `f`-carrying assignment once, as a
function of which of its factors are in `S`. Then a variant's solution set is the
intersection of those conditions. Thirty-one separate developments is the wrong
shape.

**Method note.** The statement is a conjunction over all sixteen assignments, so
a condition read off one assignment is necessary, not sufficient. More than one
assignment can constrain `f`, and the solution set is the intersection.

**Method note.** For a **fixed** `f` the sixteen assignments are decidable. The
quantification over `f` is not — `f` ranges over an infinite set — so each
characterization needs a proof, and every witness must be checked by the kernel
rather than asserted.

1	Complete the task below in this repository.
2	
3	It already contains the definitions, three tools, and this file. Nothing else.
4	Do not add a lake project, a lakefile, or any dependency.
5	
6	This is a **verification** task, not a discovery task. Several statements below
7	were computed in Python and are stated as targets. Python is not proof. Your job
8	is to settle them with the Lean kernel.
9	
10	**If the kernel disagrees with any stated target, the kernel is right. Report the
11	disagreement as the result and do not adjust the statement to make it pass.**
12	
13	## The definitions
14	
15	Already in `lean/Core.lean`, reproduced here so this file is self-contained. Do
16	not redesign them and do not reconstruct the index assignments.
17	
18	**`lean/Core.lean` is the authority. If this block and that file ever disagree,
19	the file wins and the disagreement is a defect to report.** `deriving
20	DecidableEq` on `GZ` is present so `decide` works on `GZ` equalities; if it
21	causes trouble, replace it with a hand-written instance rather than dropping it.
22	
23	**It compiles.** Verified against Lean 4.22.0 core, zero imports, `EXIT=0`.
24	Confirm that yourself as step one rather than taking it on trust.
25	
26	```lean
27	structure GZ where
28	  re : Int
29	  im : Int
30	  deriving DecidableEq
31	
32	def zero : GZ := ⟨0, 0⟩
33	def one  : GZ := ⟨1, 0⟩
34	def I    : GZ := ⟨0, 1⟩
35	
36	def add (z w : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re + w.re, z.im + w.im⟩
37	def neg (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨-z.re, -z.im⟩
38	def mul (z w : GZ) : GZ :=
39	  ⟨z.re * w.re - z.im * w.im, z.re * w.im + z.im * w.re⟩
40	def conj (z : GZ) : GZ := ⟨z.re, -z.im⟩
41	
42	/-- The symbol. One free parameter `f`, carried on a single index pattern;
43	    `one` on the other admissible patterns; `zero` off the gate. -/
44	def Fs (f : GZ) (a b c d x y : Int) : GZ :=
45	  if x = (a + b) % 2 ∧ y = (b + c) % 2 ∧ d = (a + b + c) % 2 then
46	    (if a = 1 ∧ b = 1 ∧ c = 1 then f else one)
47	  else zero
48	
49	def pentLhs (f : GZ) (a b c d : Int) : GZ :=
50	  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
51	  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2; let u := (b + c) % 2
52	  mul (mul (Fs f a b c y x u) (Fs f a u d t y v)) (Fs f b c d v u w)
53	
54	def pentRhs (f : GZ) (a b c d : Int) : GZ :=
55	  let x := (a + b) % 2; let y := (x + c) % 2; let t := (y + d) % 2
56	  let w := (c + d) % 2; let v := (b + w) % 2
57	  mul (Fs f x c d t y w) (Fs f a b w t x v)
58	
59	def pentagonHolds (f : GZ) : Prop :=
60	  ∀ a b c d : Int, (a = 0 ∨ a = 1) → (b = 0 ∨ b = 1) → (c = 0 ∨ c = 1) →
61	    (d = 0 ∨ d = 1) → pentLhs f a b c d = pentRhs f a b c d
62	```
63	
64	`pentLhs` has three `Fs` factors and `pentRhs` has two. Label them:
65	
66	    L1 = Fs f a b c y x u
67	    L2 = Fs f a u d t y v
68	    L3 = Fs f b c d v u w
69	    R1 = Fs f x c d t y w
70	    R2 = Fs f a b w t x v
71	
72	## Part 0 — what the object actually is
73	
74	Everything below this point, and everything said about the object anywhere in
75	this file, rests on properties of `GZ` that **the package asserts and does not
76	prove.** Establish them first. They are ordinary and they are all reachable.
77	
78	- `mul` is associative and commutative. **`pentLhs` writes `mul (mul A B) C` and
79	  nothing in the package licenses that grouping.** The statement is well-defined
80	  either way because it fixes its own parentheses — but no reasoning may
81	  reassociate it until this exists.
82	- `one` is a two-sided identity for `mul`.
83	- `conj` satisfies `conj (mul z w) = mul (conj z) (conj w)`, and `conj (conj z) = z`.
84	  **This file describes `conj` as a ring automorphism. That is a claim about the
85	  object and it is unproved until you prove it.**
86	- `one ≠ neg one`. Without it, a two-element solution set might be one element.
87	- `Fs` really can return `zero`: exhibit arguments where the gate fails. **If the
88	  `else zero` branch were unreachable it would be dead code in the definition
89	  under study**, and dead code is where an error hides unseen.
90	
91	**A note on how, because it is not obvious and cost an hour to find.** `ring`
92	does not exist here — it is Mathlib. `omega` is linear and will not close
93	`conj (mul z w) = mul (conj z) (conj w)`. What does work is a local
94	normalisation set: `Int.add_mul`, `Int.mul_add`, `Int.sub_mul`, `Int.mul_sub`,
95	`Int.mul_assoc`, `Int.mul_comm`, `Int.mul_left_comm`, `Int.add_assoc`,
96	`Int.add_comm`, `Int.add_left_comm`, `Int.neg_mul`, `Int.mul_neg`,
97	`Int.sub_eq_add_neg`, `Int.neg_add`, `Int.neg_neg` — declared `attribute [local
98	simp]`, after which `cases` then `simp [mul]` closes all of them.
99	
100	**That set is the whole automation budget for this part. Do not raise it without
101	saying why.**
102	
103	## Part A — the gate
104	
105	**Target.** For every one of the sixteen assignments with `a b c d ∈ {0,1}`, all
106	five factors satisfy the `if` condition in `Fs`. No factor is ever `zero`.
107	
108	Prove it as a theorem per factor, or one theorem covering all five, quantified
109	over the sixteen assignments with a live-instance count.
110	
111	## Part B — the exponent table
112	
113	For each of the sixteen assignments, each factor evaluates to `f` or to `one`.
114	Produce the table: assignment, which of L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 give `f`, and the
115	resulting powers on each side.
116	
117	Emit it as kernel-checked theorems, not as `#eval` output. Something that fails
118	to compile if the table is wrong.
119	
120	## Part C — the characterization
121	
122	**Target.** `pentagonHolds f ↔ mul f f = one`.
123	
124	**Target.** `mul f f = one ↔ (f = one ∨ f = neg one)`, over `GZ`.
125	
126	Both directions of both. The second is a statement about `Int`, so it needs a
127	real argument, not `decide` — `f.re` and `f.im` are unbounded.
128	
129	## Part D — the thirty-two cases
130	
131	For **every** subset `S ⊆ {L1, L2, L3, R1, R2}` — all thirty-two, the empty one
132	included — let `pentagonHoldsσ S f` be the same statement with `conj` applied to
133	the **value** of each factor in `S`, that is `conj (Fs f …)` in place of
134	`Fs f …` for exactly those factors. `S = ∅` is the identity substitution and
135	recovers Part C's statement.
136	
137	**Characterize all thirty-two the same way Part C characterizes one of them:** an
138	explicit condition on `f.re` and `f.im`, proved. Present them as a table of
139	thirty-two rows.
140	
141	**Do not treat the empty subset as a baseline.** Asking whether a variant is
142	*Same, Wider or Narrower than the original* privileges the original as the
143	origin, and nothing justifies that — it is one of thirty-two, distinguished only
144	by having been written down first. Report the thirty-two conditions and, if some
145	coincide, say which and why.
146	
147	**Every partition of the table is equally reportable.** If all thirty-two rows
148	carry the same condition, that is the result and should be stated flatly. If they
149	split, that is the result. Report what the kernel settles and do not editorialize
150	about it anywhere in this repository.
151	
152	**Structural fact, verified, and it reframes the whole part.** Because `Fs`
153	returns `f` or `one` or `zero`, and `conj` fixes the latter two:
154	
155	    conj (Fs f a b c d x y)  =  Fs (conj f) a b c d x y
156	
157	**So a "twist" is not a new operation on the equation. It is substituting
158	`conj f` for `f` in selected factor positions.** Prove this first; it makes
159	every case a substitution rather than a wrapper, and it is the honest way to
160	see what the thirty-two are.
161	
162	**Method note — parameterize, do not enumerate.** Thirty-two separate
163	developments is the wrong shape and will not fit. Introduce a flag per factor
164	and define the variant once:
165	
166	    def tw (b : Bool) (z : GZ) : GZ := if b then conj z else z
167	
168	Then `pentLhsV`, `pentRhsV` and `pentagonHoldsV` take five `Bool`s, and **all
169	thirty-two cases — the original included — are one theorem** whose proof
170	case-splits on the flags. That formulation has been checked to typecheck and to
171	reduce correctly; see the feasibility note below for how far it was taken.
172

**The toolchain was gone from this container.** No `lean` on PATH, no binary anywhere. I reinstalled 4.22.0 (no `zstd` on this host — the tarball had to go through Python) and sanity-checked the kernel both directions before trusting anything to it. The alternative was restating last pass's results from the summary of last pass, which is Class A.

**I retracted my own last-turn claim.** C153 said the toolbox and the carrier together made P1 onward *"impossible to state."* That is false. This compiles, zero imports, `EXIT=0`:

- a hand-declared `CRing` class
- the eight-parameter symbol and the pentagon generic over it
- invertibility as `∃ u, mul p u = one` — **no division needed, which is the step I missed**
- instantiated at `GZ`, `Int`, `Fin 2`, `Fin 8`, and `Int[ε]/ε²`

So P1, P2 and P5b are all expressible under the constraint I had just declared fatal to them. What zero imports actually removes is automation, not expressive range. The one real gap is `Rat` — not a core identifier, so `−1/4` needs an import or a hand-rolled carrier. **The carrier is what confines this to one ring, not the import list.**

Two things that were predictions are now kernel facts: `x*x = 1` has **one** root in `Fin 2` and **four** in `Fin 8`; `Int[ε]/ε²` has a non-zero nilpotent. The ring where the solution set changes shape rather than size was two lines away the whole time.

Also settled, zero axioms, with a negative control and a live-instance witness: `conj (Fs f a b c d x y) = Fs (conj f) a b c d x y`. A twist is a substitution, not a wrapper.

**Three defects entered against myself this pass:**

- The Part D baseline edit left the heading reading *thirty-one* while its body said *thirty-two* — C134 recommitted three passes after C134. No gate in the package reads prose for internal agreement; second defect from that gap.

P0 withholds the Part D answer so the model running it can't optimize toward a stated conclusion. **That blind does not extend to you** — `plan.md` §1.3 states the computed answer, and you have read it. The no-answer-in-spec discipline protects the runner, not the reader of the output. If you want a genuine blind on the interpretation step, the person reading `RESULTS.md` needs to be someone who hasn't seen `plan.md`.
